evidenceBoundary: Local deterministic fixtures and machine-local wall-clock guard assertions only. No cloud inference, production traffic, multi-user/DAU simulator, or cross-machine benchmark comparison was used.
scope: One developer's repository indexing, context assembly, and desktop run-inspection projection. Multi-user throughput and fairness are deliberately out of scope.

coverage: 1,000,000+ line deterministic repository initial index, symbol/dependency/text lookup, 32K context-pack retrieval, one-file incremental refresh, and repeated-query reuse
context windows at 16K, 32K, 64K, and 128K with provenance deduplication, history compaction, current-diff prioritization, and external-HEAD refresh
100,000 candidate files / 1,000,000 symbols bounded before provider transmission with sensitive-path exclusion
1,000 tool events, 500 file changes, and 200 token events projected from a replay duplicated in input without double-counting
100,500-line diff truncated to at most 2,000 rendered review lines

proven: The tested single-user repository intelligence path avoids an obvious million-line indexing/query/context-pack regression under its explicit local guard bounds.
Incremental refresh reparses one changed file in the fixture, and repeated symbol lookup uses the indexed state rather than requiring a full repository rebuild.
Context and run-inspection projections remain bounded at their tested synthetic input sizes and do not duplicate replayed events or usage.
Sensitive .env-like paths are excluded before the tested provider request is assembled.
notProven: Portable latency, CPU, memory, disk, startup, or battery figures. The suite asserts local upper bounds but does not publish the machine-specific sample values.
Performance on a real customer repository, an actual million-symbol code graph, a packaged Electron process, or a long-running browser/terminal session.
Multi-user throughput, fairness, DAU capacity, hosted scaling, or provider-service latency; these are outside R27's single-user scope.
requiredNextEvidence: For a publishable performance claim, capture versioned hardware/OS/runtime details, repeated raw samples, p50/p95 distributions, peak RSS/CPU/disk data, repository characteristics, cold/warm cache state, and explicit regression thresholds. Keep the run single-user unless scope is explicitly expanded.
